dict.string: Alviss connects to the mail server you configure. If that server runs on your local network, iOS asks for this permission.
Alviss uses the camera so you can take a photo and add it to a note.
Alviss records a voice memo only when you start one. The recording stays as a file in your vault; it is not sent anywhere.

Alviss asks for your position only when you press the place button while writing a journal entry. The coordinates are written into that entry and nowhere else; nothing is tracked and nothing is sent anywhere.

Alviss never asks for your position in the background and never tracks you. It asks only while you are using the app, when you press the place button in a journal entry, and the coordinates go into that entry and nowhere else.
Alviss accesses your photo library so you can add a picture to a note.
Alviss can save a photo when you add it to a note.
Alviss shows the calendars of this device next to your notes and creates the events you add from a note. Full access is needed to read and write them.
Alviss shows your reminder lists as task lists next to your notes and checks off or creates reminders from there.
